name: The 19 WritingStyle records live before the reading passes began

terms.note: [UnderReview] Coined name (the skill's own example of what is not allowed). Original AI-authored corpus, already pulled for rework by the curator note. No body of work by named hands stands behind it, so there is nothing to credit. Archived 2026-09-08. The leaf pass attached it to plain-english on 2026-09-09 and removed it the same day on reading this row: an Archived record with nothing to credit does not belong on a cell. cellId names plain-english because that is the register it was written in and the cell exists; the earlier value named a Technical reports cell (LCGFT gf2015026093) that has never been created, and if that cell is made this row moves to it.
[UnderReview] One writer, honestly named and credited (Austen, 1811–1817). A manifestation; attached under Novels of manners (B5 item 12, LCGFT gf2014026458).
[Archived] Already Archived (superseded 2026-07-06). Coined name; stays archived. Its content lives on in the Darwin, White and Field notes records.

[Archived] Already Archived (superseded 2026-07-06). Coined name; stays archived. Its content lives on in the Dana, Slocum and Ship's log records. Cell not yet created; attach when its LCGFT pass lands.

[UnderReview] Public lecture-demonstration tradition. Attached 2026-09-09 to the Royal Institution Christmas Lectures leaf, which the reference names Faraday as giving nineteen of. The earlier cellId named a Lectures cell that was never created.
[UnderReview] One writer, honestly named (Pepys, 1660s). A manifestation under Diaries (LCGFT gf2014026085), a cell for a later LCGFT pass. Cell not yet created; attach when its LCGFT pass lands.

[UnderReview] Epistolary advice tradition. Attached 2026-09-09 to the Courtesy books leaf, which the reference names his Letters to His Son as the last traditional English example of. The earlier cellId named a Personal correspondence cell that was never created.

[UnderReview] One writer, honestly named (Beeton, Book of Household Management, 1861). The register is the recipe: ingredients, quantities, mode, time, cost. A manifestation under Cookbooks (LCGFT gf2011026169); Handbooks and manuals (gf2014026109) is the broader alternative. Cell not yet created; attach when its LCGFT pass lands.

[UnderReview] One writer, honestly named (Post, Etiquette, 1922). LCGFT has no etiquette term; the nearest is Handbooks and manuals (gf2014026109). Wikidata 'courtesy book' (Q5178486) is the genre name if a narrower cell is wanted. Cell not yet created; attach when its LCGFT pass lands.

[UnderReview] One writer, honestly named (Strunk, The Elements of Style, 1918). A manifestation under Style manuals (LCGFT gf2014026183), a cell for a later LCGFT pass. Cell not yet created; attach when its LCGFT pass lands.

[UnderReview] Stoic self-address tradition. Attached 2026-09-09 to the Hypomnemata leaf, the Greek practice of the personal notebook kept for rereading. The earlier cellId named a Meditations cell that was never created.

[UnderReview] Two writers and a translator, honestly named (Grimm, Taylor translation, 1823). Pass 1 proposes Folk tales (LCGFT gf2014026344, the parent term) with this record as its manifestation; when Fairy tales (gf2014026329) is proposed in a later slice the pointer moves to that narrower cell.

[UnderReview] One writer, honestly named (Twain, The Innocents Abroad, 1869). A manifestation under Travel writing (LCGFT gf2014026200), a cell for a later LCGFT pass. Cell not yet created; attach when its LCGFT pass lands.
[UnderReview] One writer, honestly named (Darwin, The Voyage of the Beagle, 1839). Attached under Field notes (B5 item 13); Travel writing is the alternative by form.
[UnderReview] One writer, honestly named (White, The Natural History of Selborne, 1789). Attached under Field notes (B5 item 13) by content; Personal correspondence is the alternative by form.

Attach under Travel writing until a Logbooks cell exists. Cell not yet created; attach when its LCGFT pass lands.
